title: Laboratory validation of enzyme-immunoassays for the non-invasive quantification of reproductive and stress hormone in amphibians
protocol: Determine concentrations of urinary corticosterone using polyclonal anticorticosterone antiserum CJM06 diluted 1:45,000.
Use horseradish peroxidase conjugated corticosterone label diluted 1:120,000 for the assay.
Utilize corticosterone standards ranging from 1.56 to 400 pg/well for calibration.
Coat 96 well Nunc maxi-SorpTM plates with 50 µL of antibody in ELISA coating buffer.
Incubate the coated plates overnight at 4°C.
Dilute standards, internal controls, and urine samples in enzyme immunoassay buffer.
Add 50 µL of diluted standards, controls, and samples to each well according to the assay plate map.
Add 50 µL of horseradish peroxidase label to each well.
Incubate the plates at room temperature for 2 hours.
Wash the plates.
Add 50 µL of substrate solution to each well.
Incubate the plates until the optical density of zero wells reads between 0.7 and 1, typically after at least 10 minutes at room temperature.
Add 50 µL of stopping solution based on visual inspection of the plates.
Subtract blank absorbance from each reading to account for non-specific binding.
Generate frog urine samples.
Fit a regression line using the method of least squares.
Determine hormone metabolite concentrations in the frog urine samples using the regression line.
Determine creatinine concentrations in frog urine using the Jaffe method.
Calculate urinary hormone metabolite concentrations in relation to urinary creatinine concentrations.
Present all steroidal concentrations as mean ± standard error (SE) pg/μg Cr.
